headers.review_note: All five fallback function declarations and aliases are now included by forced fallback extraction.
Compatibility includes only; no public operations, fields, enums or macros in the native extraction. Standard scalar types have Wren value equivalents subject to documented exact Number limits.

values.array_list.wren: List / Map / String.split and join; script sort comparators
values.array_list.reason: Native capacity, owned char pointers, cached name keys, insertion sentinels, take/free and C comparison callbacks are storage mechanisms. Wren owns values; List operations and script comparators supply collection behavior. A native sorted-unique insertion does not imply that arbitrary List values are automatically sorted or unique.

values.name_value_list.wren: List / Map keyed by Text.caselessKey where native canonical caseless equality is required
values.name_value_list.reason: Native capacity, owned char pointers, cached name keys, insertion sentinels, take/free and C comparison callbacks are storage mechanisms. Wren owns values; List operations and script comparators supply collection behavior. A native sorted-unique insertion does not imply that arbitrary List values are automatically sorted or unique. A raw String-keyed Wren Map is case-sensitive; callers requiring native name equality must use the explicit Text.caselessKey operation rather than assuming Map changes language equality.

values.str_list.wren: List / Map / String.split and join; script sort comparators
values.str_list.reason: Native capacity, owned char pointers, cached name keys, insertion sentinels, take/free and C comparison callbacks are storage mechanisms. Wren owns values; List operations and script comparators supply collection behavior. A native sorted-unique insertion does not imply that arbitrary List values are automatically sorted or unique.

utility.base64.reason: No general byte Base64 encoder/decoder is exported. Internal token serialization is not a public codec; implementing the algorithm in a script is not an existing equivalent.

utility.hex.reason: File digests return raw bytes; no general byte-to-hex / hex-to-byte codec or digit decoder is exported.

utility.cipher.wren: Menu.setEncryption is a fixed BBS-list workflow, not a cipher API
utility.cipher.reason: No general cipher support query or byte encryption/decryption operation exists. Native legacy algorithm enums describe provider/read compatibility; this finding does not propose enabling legacy writers.

utility.kdf.reason: No general PBKDF2/scrypt operation or parameter validation API. Fixed list encryption is a consumer, not a mapping of arbitrary KDF input/output.

utility.digest.reason: Only two file digest algorithms are exposed. SHA-256/384/512, generic byte-buffer digest input and digest-size query are absent. File methods are grant-confined and return raw digest bytes.
utility.digest.vm: menu/connected grant owners; no file opening in picker VM

utility.crypto.reason: No general random-byte operation, provider version query, or crypto-status taxonomy is exported. List workflow errors do not expose every provider result. Secret clearing remains native ownership, classified separately.

utility.crypto-provider.reason: Reports the selected native crypto provider name in the build information; no promise of a structured provider object.

utility.crypto-clear.reason: A Wren String is immutable VM-managed storage. Clearing a native secret buffer belongs to the native owner and cannot promise erasure of arbitrary Wren copies.
utility.crypto-clear.vm: same VM as the owning API

utility.md5-state.reason: The streaming MD5 state/block owner belongs to native APC validation. File.md5 now uses st_digest instead. The general byte/stream digest utility omission is recorded in utility.digest; raw state pointers are not a separate script object.

host.dynamic_library.reason: The application owns these native lifetimes and synchronization. Script execution is single-threaded and cooperatively scheduled with Fiber/Operation/Timer; scripts cannot create C threads, access raw synchronization objects, or load arbitrary native symbols. Exposing a second owner would bypass the VM/lifetime boundary.

host.st_event.reason: The application owns these native lifetimes and synchronization. Script execution is single-threaded and cooperatively scheduled with Fiber/Operation/Timer; scripts cannot create C threads, access raw synchronization objects, or load arbitrary native symbols. Exposing a second owner would bypass the VM/lifetime boundary.

host.st_semaphore.reason: The application owns these native lifetimes and synchronization. Script execution is single-threaded and cooperatively scheduled with Fiber/Operation/Timer; scripts cannot create C threads, access raw synchronization objects, or load arbitrary native symbols. Exposing a second owner would bypass the VM/lifetime boundary.

host.st_threads.reason: The application owns these native lifetimes and synchronization. Script execution is single-threaded and cooperatively scheduled with Fiber/Operation/Timer; scripts cannot create C threads, access raw synchronization objects, or load arbitrary native symbols. Exposing a second owner would bypass the VM/lifetime boundary.

errors.io.reason: IOErr exposes all 38 stable shared native I/O codes in every VM. FileErr was removed without an alias; FileError remains the filesystem error type. MenuError separates portable codes from raw generic native failures instead of interpreting legacy -1 as invalidArgument. Host errno/Windows translators remain host mechanisms.

errors.io-translation.reason: Platform errno/Windows error conversion happens at the native failure boundary; script errors carry portable code and captured errno rather than translating ambient process error state.
errors.io-translation.vm: same VM as the owning API

language.preferences.reason: Ordered preferred UI language tags become a Wren List of Strings; count is List.count and release is VM-owned. Native discovery allocation stays private.

utility.ascii.wren: no exact general ASCII helper API
utility.ascii.reason: Unicode-aware Text comparisons and standard String operations are available, but do not have the exact ASCII-only trimming, span and case semantics of every native helper. These implementation utilities are not a required portability API for scripts; broader relevance remains a scope decision.

time.clock.reason: Timer.now returns monotonic seconds from st_time_monotonic_ms; Timer.after supplies cooperative waits. Standard Wren System.clock supplies process CPU seconds. Nanosecond precision is not promised by these floating-second APIs; native deadline records and UTC condition-variable deadlines are host scheduling mechanisms.

time.deadline.reason: Deadline storage, infinite sentinel, remaining-time arithmetic and UTC timeout conversion implement native waits. Scripts use Timer operations and do not own condition-variable deadlines.
time.deadline.vm: same VM as the owning API

utility.conversion.wren: typed model setters consume values; no full generic conversion API
utility.conversion.reason: Native strict int64/uint64/bool/double parsing and duration/date parsing/formatting have no exact general script equivalent. Num.fromString and toString have different syntax/ranges; binary64 cannot represent all native 64-bit integers. Typed settings use these internally. This is an omitted utility scope decision, not justification for changing Wren Number.

utility.estimates.reason: Native human-readable estimates are exposed with explicit exact-number bounds for byte counts. These methods do not expose exact duration/date serialization.
utility.estimates.vm: same VM as the owning API

paths.application.reason: Application startup resolves and prepares configuration/list/cache/key/script/theme roots. Scripts receive locations or confined directory capabilities where appropriate; they cannot reinitialize process path ownership, swap every root, or mint grants by writing path overrides. Relevant fileLocations output is descriptive, not arbitrary file authority.
paths.application.vm: menu for global locations; connected for per-entry grants

consent.signer.reason: Signing key generation and token authentication are native consent authority. Scripts may retain/reopen issued capabilities but cannot mint valid arbitrary-path grants or receive the signing key.
consent.signer.vm: menu/connected grant owners; no file opening in picker VM

config.ini.wren: Profile / Settings / ThemeDocument are typed consumers only
config.ini.reason: No general INI document/section API is exported: parsing/serialization, root/section/key CRUD, typed getters/setters, style options and bit/enum/list conversion remain native. Typed application models cover their own workflows but do not map arbitrary INI documents. NFC host-text policy remains unchanged.

list.crypto.reason: The owned BBS-list writer supports plain/AES-128/AES-256/ChaCha20 and current-password rewrite. Writing still fixes scrypt block/parallelism to defaults, and generic encrypted INI streams are not exposed; those scope questions remain open. setEncryption now preserves native mutation failures through MenuError. Metadata, legacy naming and the Settings effective KDF policy retain their earlier approved resolutions.
resolved_subclaims: Loaded format, cipher, key size, actual KDF parameters and rewrite recommendation are copied into an immutable snapshot.
Legacy cipher display names and named enum values are accurate; unsupported password-change actions are hidden.
Menu.setEncryption returns null/MenuError and preserves available native reasons without new writer options or storage policy.

profile.fields.wren: Profile + DirectoryEntry + Session and enum namespaces
profile.fields.reason: Editable connection configuration is Profile; persistent name/id/source/added/connected/calls/sortOrder belongs to DirectoryEntry; runtime connection state belongs to Session. Palette length and fingerprint length come from script value lengths. Typed encoding/script setters replace native persistence parsers; defaults intentionally have no scripts. Source classification is only the two-value profile source contract here; the richer BBS source issue is separate. Fixed buffer capacities are validation limits, not separate values to allocate.
profile.fields.vm: menu and connected; persistence/menu enumeration only in menu

profile.ownership.wren: Profile.copy; VM-backed views and host model owners
profile.ownership.reason: Native init/dispose/copy and cached ghost-program interpretation implement the value/view lifetime. Script copy returns an independent value; native pointers are not transferred.
profile.ownership.vm: same VM as the owning API

bbs.workflow.reason: The menu owns a merged BBS model; enumeration/find/count use Wren Lists, identity and generations stay attached to foreign handles, sort field catalogs and profiles supply native ordering. Per-entry/default edits are validated typed operations. Connection recording is performed by the application. Limits are surfaced through canAppendEntry and validated mutation. Cache paths and picker keys remain bound to the owning entry, not arbitrary filesystem open authority.

bbs.provenance.reason: DirectoryEntry.type / profile.source still collapses the native four source kinds to personal versus system, and source_name is not exposed for entries. Scripts cannot identify which named list provided an entry or inspect shadowed provenance. BBSListSource enum values and load-diagnostic source names are now separately covered; that does not resolve entry provenance.

bbs.cache-result.reason: Native cache_status is secondary optional housekeeping after primary list success. Wren intentionally reports primary success without this status: the user approved that cache maintenance is optional and must not determine mutation success. No cache/store/write-policy changes or new result API are required. Coverage remains Partial because this native status is intentionally omitted; primary result fidelity is accounted separately under model-mutation-results, whose Settings disk-reload and emoji-result subclaims remain open.

bbs.diagnostics.reason: On request, snapshots copy all four native diagnostic fields in native order, with strict UTF-8/NFC owned names and a lazily constructed MenuError preserving portable status. Snapshots survive GC/reloads, grant no authority, and are distinct from failed candidates. No native API was added. The bundled menu shows one scrollable warning summary after successful loading and continues if warning retrieval fails. Missing optional sources retain native silent-skip policy.

bbs.refresh-detail.reason: Menu exposes refresh of a configured list but not native per-item queued/active/complete/failed state, phase, received/total/total_known, status and outcome progress records. The synchronous menu workflow does not provide an observer callback.

bbs.transaction-owner.wren: menu BBS model and application startup/connection recording
bbs.transaction-owner.reason: Open/replacement/close, raw borrowed entries, native compare callbacks/cache keys and orphan-cache sweeping belong to the menu model transaction/lifetime. Scripts use typed mutations and entry-owned cache grants; they do not instantiate parallel application BBS owners. The cache ownership marker filename is a reserved host mechanism; cache grants reject access to it.

settings.model.wren: Menu.settings / Settings apply/save/reload; Menu webLists/sortProfiles/fonts; Emoji recent entries
settings.model.reason: Editable settings are draft values with validated typed setters. Menu owns web-list/sort-profile/custom-font collections; MenuFont setFile takes a granted File. Native collection count/index becomes List/count; recent emoji uses Emoji accessors. Theme selection is Menu-owned rather than a second raw Settings setter. Scaling modes combine native blocky/external flags. Raw global installation, disposal and startup snapshots remain host mechanisms. Specific omitted settings are classified separately.
settings.model.vm: menu; emoji access in core VMs

settings.window-state.reason: scaling_factor, window_width, window_height and left_justify have no Settings property. Some are remembered frontend state, but text alignment is also user policy. They must not be declared covered merely because the host persists them; whether to expose window state versus policy remains a scope decision.

settings.transfer-timeouts.reason: Transfer success/failure keypress timeout settings have no Settings getters/setters despite being native persisted user policy.

settings.kdf-legacy.reason: Approved intentional typed policy: kdfShift reports the effective rewrite cost (8..20), with fallback 15 for unsupported old stored strings. It is not a lossless representation of persisted text. Untouched specifications remain preserved. Actual loaded-file KDF metadata is separately available through Menu.encryptionInfo. The user rejected a raw kdfSpec property and nullable getter.

settings.lifecycle.wren: Settings snapshots and menu application transaction
settings.lifecycle.reason: Native global storage, init/dispose/copy/load/install/shutdown and resolved list_path are owned by application startup and transactional Settings application. Draft baseline is conflict-detection state, not another user field; menu APIs own font draft lifetime. Stored list path is editable through Settings.listPath.

themes.documents.reason: Theme metadata/styles/glyphs become script values, with List counts and present/mode information in document rows. ThemeDocument provides create/open/metadata/CRUD/preview/undo/redo/import/save/dirty and reports document conflicts through its operation results. Local/cloud catalogs expose validation errors and selection/cache/delete workflows; parsed cloud content is obtainable through copyCloudTheme and themeData rather than a borrowed C pointer.
themes.documents.vm: menu editing; core VMs for active/default theme data

themes.cloud-origin.reason: Catalog rows omit the native source URI and expected SHA-256. Downloads and verification remain host-owned, but scripts cannot inspect or display that provenance. Parsed theme ownership is separately represented by copyCloudTheme rather than missing because a pointer is absent.

themes.manager-lifetime.wren: application theme manager; transactional Settings preparation
themes.manager-lifetime.reason: Manager create/free, prepare/install/free and raw cache refresh policy coordinate the one active theme and rollback. Scripts preview/select/edit through that owner; they cannot install a separate manager into a VM.

files.transaction-lock.reason: Persistent sidecar advisory locks protect application data updates. Scripts use transactional typed model saves; they do not receive arbitrary-path sidecar locks or hold model locks across a yielding Fiber.

files.mapping.wren: File digest/image decoders and native readers
files.mapping.reason: Read-only memory mapping is an implementation of granted-file reads, hashing and decoding. Wren owns immutable byte Strings rather than borrowed mapped pointers; no independent mapped-memory lifetime or concurrent-modification contract is added.
files.mapping.vm: menu/connected grant owners; no file opening in picker VM

files.grants.reason: Size/position/seek/mtime, granted opening, removal, child creation and atomic replacement are represented with native portable FileError details. Native parent-directory creation is performed inside grant/model operations, not arbitrary-path authority. Files use byte Strings for payloads; textual paths remain strict UTF-8 NFC. Link/other classification and standalone truncation are separately assessed.
files.grants.vm: menu/connected grant owners; no file opening in picker VM

files.rename-copy.reason: No granted rename or native copy-file operation exists. Read/write/delete cannot promise atomic rename or the native copy mode/mtime behavior.
files.rename-copy.vm: menu/connected grant owners; no file opening in picker VM

files.truncate.reason: The binding offers reads/writes/seek and size inspection, but no explicit truncation to a chosen length. Creating/replacing a file is not equivalent to truncating an existing granted stream at an arbitrary length.
files.truncate.vm: menu/connected grant owners; no file opening in picker VM

files.link-metadata.reason: Native fs_get_link_info distinguishes link/other/file/directory without following the link. Script listing exposes only directory versus file-like entries and does not offer an lstat-equivalent kind query. Native modified time and size do have corresponding metadata. Directory grants deliberately reject/omit links to avoid following ungranted paths; the missing lstat metadata is an observation of that security boundary, not a request to grant link traversal.
files.link-metadata.vm: menu/connected grant owners; no file opening in picker VM

files.mkdir-internal.reason: Recursive parent preparation is performed by the owning model/application before writes. Directory.createDir creates one confined child; arbitrary path creation outside a grant is intentionally unavailable.
files.mkdir-internal.vm: menu/connected grant owners; no file opening in picker VM

paths.picker.reason: Picker-only path resolution/join and path metadata cover the trusted user-selection workflow; no general Path utility namespace exports all native separator/basename/component/root/parent/absolute/user-expansion operations in other VMs. Pure path calculation would not itself grant file access; lack of a generic helper is an unresolved utility scope decision, not a reason to permit arbitrary file opening.

serial.connection.wren: Profile baud/data/stop/parity/flow configuration; Menu.serialRates; active Conn
serial.connection.reason: Serial reads/writes/configuration use the active connection and per-entry profile, not an arbitrary device object. Open/close and transport queues are host-owned. Device rates and ordinary profile parity/flow choices have script equivalents.

serial.lines.reason: Native DTR/RTS setters, modem CTS/DSR/RING/DCD query and DTR_DSR flow choice have no script counterpart. General device ownership remains host-controlled; whether active-connection line controls should be exposed is a separate scope decision.
serial.lines.vm: same VM as the owning API

serial.transport-owner.reason: Application connection owns serial handle and transport shutdown. Scripts send through Conn/Session and cannot open a second arbitrary serial device or close/configure the borrowed native handle underneath its worker.
serial.transport-owner.vm: same VM as the owning API

transport.connection_shell_codec.reason: Socket handles, worker mutexes/queues, stream interrupts, resolver callbacks, raw short I/O, urgent marks, shutdown halves, shell codec acknowledgement and optional-provider state implement the owning connection. A connected VM may operate its current connection; it cannot start arbitrary additional network connections or receive a second raw socket owner. Address-family selection is in Profile.addressFamily. Native connect timeout/diagnostics are host setup policy rather than a generic script TCP client.
transport.connection_shell_codec.vm: application ownership; connected VM uses Conn

transport.connection_stream.reason: Socket handles, worker mutexes/queues, stream interrupts, resolver callbacks, raw short I/O, urgent marks, shutdown halves, shell codec acknowledgement and optional-provider state implement the owning connection. A connected VM may operate its current connection; it cannot start arbitrary additional network connections or receive a second raw socket owner. Address-family selection is in Profile.addressFamily. Native connect timeout/diagnostics are host setup policy rather than a generic script TCP client.
transport.connection_stream.vm: application ownership; connected VM uses Conn

transport.connection_tcp.reason: Socket handles, worker mutexes/queues, stream interrupts, resolver callbacks, raw short I/O, urgent marks, shutdown halves, shell codec acknowledgement and optional-provider state implement the owning connection. A connected VM may operate its current connection; it cannot start arbitrary additional network connections or receive a second raw socket owner. Address-family selection is in Profile.addressFamily. Native connect timeout/diagnostics are host setup policy rather than a generic script TCP client.
transport.connection_tcp.vm: application ownership; connected VM uses Conn

transport.socket.reason: Socket handles, worker mutexes/queues, stream interrupts, resolver callbacks, raw short I/O, urgent marks, shutdown halves, shell codec acknowledgement and optional-provider state implement the owning connection. A connected VM may operate its current connection; it cannot start arbitrary additional network connections or receive a second raw socket owner. Address-family selection is in Profile.addressFamily. Native connect timeout/diagnostics are host setup policy rather than a generic script TCP client.
transport.socket.vm: application ownership; connected VM uses Conn

transport.tcp_client.reason: Socket handles, worker mutexes/queues, stream interrupts, resolver callbacks, raw short I/O, urgent marks, shutdown halves, shell codec acknowledgement and optional-provider state implement the owning connection. A connected VM may operate its current connection; it cannot start arbitrary additional network connections or receive a second raw socket owner. Address-family selection is in Profile.addressFamily. Native connect timeout/diagnostics are host setup policy rather than a generic script TCP client.
transport.tcp_client.vm: application ownership; connected VM uses Conn

connection.active.wren: Conn / WireLease / Session / Profile; SFTP / Host.sshPublicKey
connection.active.reason: Text/byte/wire send intent is preserved by owned send Operations or a WireLease. Queue-pressure and partial failure are ConnError values; there is no unsafe input-offset retry contract. Leased receive/peek/available expose the active wire under exclusive ownership. Connected/type/elapsed/queued state, SFTP provider and public-key utility have equivalents. Setup is selected through menu Profile, not constructor calls in connected scripts. The native diagnostic/setup information and binary mode controls are separately assessed.

connection.setup-owner.reason: Native connection constructors/close/request processing and setup prompt/trust/log callback pointers are managed by the application. Profile expresses endpoint/authentication/geometry. Closing Conn requests the active owner shutdown, not native destruction while workers still reference it. Shell termcap/mm_charset are derived from terminal mode/encoding; callbacks never transfer native worker ownership to Wren.

connection.setup-diagnostics.wren: host setup UI and protocol logs; ConnError for queued sends
connection.setup-diagnostics.reason: Structured native setup error code/phase/native_error/has_native_error/detail/presented and progress-state enum are not queryable as a script connection-attempt result. Host prompts/logs cover user-facing setup but do not preserve a machine-readable result for Menu.connect selection. ConnError is a different active-send error contract.

connection.binary-owner.reason: Binary negotiation switching is serialized with terminal-channel ownership and transfer transitions. Scripts request semantic text/bytes/wire send intent, not raw Telnet worker mode changes. Exposing the borrowed worker mode separately could invalidate the current owner framing.
connection.binary-owner.vm: same VM as the owning API

sftp.operations.wren: SFTP / Operation / RemoteFile / RemoteDirectory / SFTPStat / SFTPEntry / SFTPError
sftp.operations.reason: All fifteen provider operations have typed equivalents. Remote handles carry context, read/write/append rights and explicit asynchronous close state. Native request ids/result kind dispatch are Operation implementation, byte size is String.bytes.count, entry_count is List.count, full standalone stat fields have getters, and code/serverStatus/message/transient errors survive. Path inputs use host NFC text while contents/hashes remain raw bytes. Per-entry metadata omission is separately assigned.

sftp.entry-stat.reason: SFTPEntry.stat constructs a fresh immutable native SFTPStat copy only on access, exposing all six listing-time fields without another request. Scalar metadata survives provider reuse, entry collection and directory closure. Existing exact-number validation, whole-list overflow errors, unsigned 32-bit mode/UID/GID and native zero defaults are preserved. Removed entry.size/mtime have no aliases; the browser captures stat once per row. No remote resource authority or queue/grant changes.

sftp.provider-owner.wren: native active SSH provider and Operation scheduler
sftp.provider-owner.reason: Provider context/submit/poll/cancel_all and request identity/kind/raw handle are native transport and asynchronous-owner machinery. Script owners cancel Operations and close RemoteFile/RemoteDirectory rather than borrowing arbitrary numeric handles or polling the provider independently.
sftp.provider-owner.vm: same VM as the owning API

tls.owner.wren: active connection/webget TLS owners; Profile TLS policy; trusted menu UI
tls.owner.reason: TLS object allocation, socket I/O/flush/pending/terminate/close and borrowed callback lifetimes belong to the connection or downloader. Profile supplies hostname/trust anchor/client credentials/PSK/version floor. Host-controlled trust UI handles unauthenticated peer chains; scripts cannot open independent TLS transports or take over trust callbacks. Selected metadata/policy omissions are separately assigned.

tls.peer-info.wren: no active Session TLS inspection object
tls.peer-info.reason: Negotiated version/cipher, full certificate count/subject/issuer/validity/SHA-256 fingerprint/PEM and the last TLS error are not exposed for connected inspection. Profile.tlsVersionFloor is saved policy, not negotiated state; host certificate prompts are not a query API. This omission does not authorize script trust replacement.

tls.policy-options.reason: Native maximum TLS version, handshake timeout and independent PSK compatibility policy are not script-configurable. Native diagnostic records retain status/provider_status/fatal/provider/message/level; script protocol logs flatten these and do not expose the structured record. Existing supported profile policy maps the remaining ordinary options; raw callback context/pointers remain host mechanisms.
tls.policy-options.vm: same VM as the owning API

transfer.workflow.wren: Transfer upload/uploadBatch/download / snapshot / dialogs / log / done/success/abort
transfer.workflow.reason: Common protocol choices, progress text/byte counts, user duplicate-file responses and abort/completion map to the one session transfer owner. Session transfer inspection wraps native state. Starting the worker and pumping input are not separate script thread APIs. Result detail, receive-policy/streaming options, XMODEM-G selection and raw upload paths are separately recorded.

transfer.result-code.reason: The native integer completion result is reduced to success Bool and aborted Bool; startup errors use a generic abort message. Native error reasons cannot be recovered from these flags, even though a textual log may explain some failures.
transfer.result-code.vm: same VM as the owning API

transfer.xmodem-g.reason: Native XMODEM-G exists and RIP can choose it, but Transfer protocol parser offers no explicit xmodem-g choice for script-directed transfers.
transfer.xmodem-g.vm: same VM as the owning API

transfer.receive-policy.reason: Native overwrite/discard/receive_events, destination callback and begin/data/end receive mailbox support asset playback. The binding uses them internally for RIP; scripts cannot choose these modes or consume transfer bytes/events as a generic stream. Borrowed native callbacks are not appropriate to expose directly, but their usable streaming capability remains a scope decision.
transfer.receive-policy.vm: same VM as the owning API

transfer.path-authority.reason: Actual File class, VM ownership, read rights and cache-owner lifetime are checked. String sources must resolve to regular files beneath the active BBS cache or immutable configured upload-directory root; descendant links and escaping normalized paths are rejected. Every batch source is checked before any worker starts. Picker callers retain File objects instead of discarding the grant as a String.
transfer.path-authority.vm: same VM as the owning API

evidence.anchor: queue lost upload grant across VMs

transfer.path-authority.resolution: Resolved by the upload-consent follow-up. The legacy reference tree is unchanged.

transfer.worker-owner.wren: one native transfer worker owned by session
transfer.worker-owner.reason: Create/launch/start/join/destroy, transport callback/context, bounded feed/eof/input-space/take-input and CET replay pointer manage worker lifetime and channel ownership. Scripts start a Transfer and inspect progress; the host joins before releasing buffers, drains receive/replay bytes and restores terminal ownership.
transfer.worker-owner.vm: same VM as the owning API

transfer.autodetect.wren: connected terminal transfer detection and Transfer auto-pending workflow
transfer.autodetect.reason: Detector prefix bytes and size are incremental parser state held by the session. Automatic transfer dispatch surfaces through the existing Transfer workflow; a second script detector would race the channel owner.

webget.workflow.wren: Menu named web lists / cloud themes
webget.workflow.reason: Native downloads are usable only through fixed list/theme workflows. No general HTTP-to-granted-file request exposes URL/cache key/output/timeout/size/validator/TLS choices, progress or downloaded/not-modified/fresh-cache/size result. Existing workflows are not generic HTTP coverage. Whether to add any general service is a scope/trust decision; the connected VM currently cannot establish another connection.

audio.playback.reason: Wren can select allowed audio backends through Settings.audioModes and trigger terminal-protocol music/OOII sound, but cannot directly synthesize tones/waves, beep, submit PCM, create streams, choose volume/ramp/fade/crossfade/loop, drain/clear or inspect stream idle/volume. Native functional audio availability is therefore not full script audio coverage. Whether a general playback API belongs in scope remains a policy decision.

audio.engine-owner.wren: application audio runtime / libretro pull frontend
audio.engine-owner.reason: Audio engine/device lifecycle, backend selection, mix pull and stopping/joining belong to the shared application runtime, not a per-VM hardware owner. An eventual script playback API would submit to this owner.
audio.engine-owner.vm: same VM as the owning API

audio.backends.reason: Native compiled/available audio backend choices are exposed in menu configuration and applied by the native audio runtime. PCM frame/sample constants describe an unbound general playback format, separately accounted.

audio.runtime.reason: Runtime create/pull/stop/destroy/acquire and allowed-backend mask coordinate lazy device opening across CTerm/OOII and frontend ownership. Settings.audioModes supplies user policy; scripts do not borrow the audio engine pointer.

audio.decode.reason: Terminal protocols can consume sounds internally, but no script format availability query or granted-file/byte decoding to PCM is exposed. Native stream/memory inputs are not mapped by the absence of an AudioFile object.

audio.mixer.wren: native shared engine mixer and worker acknowledgement
audio.mixer.reason: Mixer pull/wait/acknowledge and stream ownership duplicate the lower implementation of audio.h, not an additional script engine. The unbound playback controls/stream behavior are recorded under audio.playback; native mixer pointers, wakeups and ownership transfers stay private.

pixels.values.wren: PixelBuffer / PixelMask / PixelBlit / PixelColor and Screen pixel methods
pixels.values.reason: Owned primary/alternate planes, dimension/count, pixel/mask read-write/fill/clone, RGB conversion, integer scale/flip/source/destination/mask descriptor choices have Wren equivalents. VM finalizers own buffers and masks. The screen is the only exported blit destination; offscreen compositing and display resampling are assessed separately.

pixels.offscreen-blit.reason: Native st_pixel_buffer_blit can composite into another PixelBuffer with clipping/mask/flips/scaling/alternate plane. Wren only exports screen-destination blit; PixelBuffer itself has no corresponding operation. Pixel-by-pixel script code is not a built-in native-equivalent operation.
pixels.offscreen-blit.vm: same VM as the owning API

pixels.display-scaler.reason: RGB output buffers and pointy/blocky scaler create/destroy/scale/region are display presentation machinery. Script PixelBuffer uses palette/RGB tagged planes; Settings.scalingMode selects frontend scaling policy rather than a second script-owned resampling pipeline.
pixels.display-scaler.vm: same VM as the owning API

pixels.decode.reason: Image inputs accept permitted byte/file forms and produce owned pixel/mask values; JXL support is explicitly queryable. CTerm-specific decoders handle protocol framing and the native renderer owns their lifetime, not a separate generic script image dialect.

pixels.cterm-decode.reason: CTerm-specific decoder variants implement its legacy wire framing. Generic script decoders expose standard PPM/PBM; a protocol adapter is owned by CTerm.
pixels.cterm-decode.vm: same VM as the owning API

fonts.catalog.reason: Script selectors adapt console-owned native registrations. Connected contexts use actual terminal identifiers/mappings, including remote variants; menu/picker catalogs retain their own registrations. Availability, extent and direct mapping queries reflect registration state. Allocation/free and raw pointer ownership stay native.

fonts.codepage-loading.reason: Explicit loading accepts Codepage; the default captures current CTerm.codepage, independent of Screen.font and including UTF-8 fallback. Native catalogs retain actual custom mappings. Connected contexts import the terminal registrations rather than CP437 copies, including shared menu consoles. Remote variants retain and restore mappings with their rasters. Unavailable mappings return null, not fabricated CP437.
fonts.codepage-loading.vm: same VM as the owning API

fonts.catalog-owner.wren: VM font catalog and console registry
fonts.catalog-owner.reason: Create/destroy and raw console/identifier conversion implement native font ownership. Script selectors are translated by the VM catalog, not raw reusable native pointers.
fonts.catalog-owner.vm: same VM as the owning API

fonts.builtin.reason: Loaded font names/mappings are available in each VM; the full built-in name/encoding catalogs are available through Menu, independently of the current geometry. Raster retrieval remains console ownership. The broken-vertical compatibility bit remains separately unbound.
fonts.builtin.vm: all VMs for loaded font metadata; menu for complete built-in catalogs

fonts.vertical-compatibility.reason: No public query reports the native broken-vertical font compatibility bit. Menu filters/name/codepage do not convey that specific metadata.
fonts.vertical-compatibility.vm: same VM as the owning API

fonts.raster-owner.reason: Native built-in raster pointer is registered/rendered by the console. Scripts use selectors and text, not borrowed static raster structs.
fonts.raster-owner.vm: same VM as the owning API

fonts.st_emoji_fonts.reason: Bundled immutable raster objects and presentation font create/destroy/storage are renderer-owned. Scripts use Font selectors, semantic Cell.ch and Emoji metadata rather than borrowing backend raster pointers. General custom raster capabilities are recorded under console.rich-font.

fonts.st_unicode_fonts.reason: Bundled immutable raster objects and presentation font create/destroy/storage are renderer-owned. Scripts use Font selectors, semantic Cell.ch and Emoji metadata rather than borrowing backend raster pointers. General custom raster capabilities are recorded under console.rich-font.

fonts.st_presentation_font.reason: Bundled immutable raster objects and presentation font create/destroy/storage are renderer-owned. Scripts use Font selectors, semantic Cell.ch and Emoji metadata rather than borrowing backend raster pointers. General custom raster capabilities are recorded under console.rich-font.

console.owner.wren: application display and logical console owners
console.owner.reason: Creation/destruction/activation, frontend ABI frame copy/map, backend config/write callbacks, native font lookup/fallback/presentation, batching/present internals and raw event queue ownership belong to the application/renderer. Menu, picker and connected VMs use their existing logical consoles. Native pointer/stride/reserved/dirty bookkeeping is not a second script-visible resource owner. Script-facing operations/fields/enums are overridden below; this is not a claim of blanket console coverage.

console.cells.reason: Semantic text/font/palette/RGB/hyperlink fields and rectangular cell operations have equivalents. Native glyph ids and resolved glyph_font are translated through text/font catalogs, not cast as Unicode scalars. Surface/Cell preserve opaque content on copying. Full style-bit editing is recorded separately.
console.cells.vm: same VM as the owning API

console.style-bits.reason: Native public style flags include underline, bold, reverse, conceal, double-height and teletext presentation controls. Wren exposes bright/blink, legacy colour attributes and readonly pixelGraphics, but no complete flag inspection/editing interface. Opaque Surface copy preserves them; that is not script control. Dirty/reserved and renderer-resolved flags remain host bookkeeping.
console.style-bits.vm: same VM as the owning API

console.operations.wren: Screen/ScreenWindow/Palette/CustomCursor/VideoFlags/Clipboard; Settings scaling/colorEmoji; Input.mouseVisible; Menu screen modes
console.operations.reason: Logical-console size/layout, text drawing/window operations, cursor shape snapshots, palette and pixel operations, screen snapshots and title/clipboard/openURL have higher-level Wren owners. Settings/menu handle user display modes. Snapshot and text-buffer releases use VM finalizers/owned Strings. Reconfigure is constrained to supported screen modes; arbitrary frontend console construction is not implied.
console.operations.vm: same VM as the owning API

console.immutable-expand.reason: ST_CONSOLE_VIDEO_EXPAND is immutable after console creation: native st_console_set_video_flags rejects changing it. Readonly VideoFlags.expand therefore matches the live native contract; this is not a missing setter. LineGraphicsExpand is independently mutable and has setters.
console.immutable-expand.vm: same VM as the owning API

console.display-controls.reason: Native wrap, blink mode, full-surface-scroll, fallback-font choice, explicit aspect ratio and fullscreen setters lack direct script control/query. Some are derived by emulation or selected screen mode and may properly stay host policy; that is a scope decision. Settings custom aspect configures a future/custom mode, not arbitrary live aspect changes. Native pointer-shape selection (default/text/link) is only used by the host hyperlink-hover owners; no generic script pointer-shape selector is exported.
console.display-controls.vm: same VM as the owning API

console.rich-font.reason: The native font descriptor can register arbitrary bitmap widths/glyph counts/strides, wide rasters, scalar and cluster mappings, coloured glyphs and fallback/decode-error glyphs. Wren only loads supported legacy font files; it cannot construct these descriptors from script data. Native mappings used by Cell text/rendering are not a general script font-builder API.
console.rich-font.vm: same VM as the owning API

console.input-events.reason: Named keys, physical press/release/repeat, committed scalars, codepage bytes and doorway keys have distinct script representations. Mouse cell/pixel coordinates, both wheel axes, buttons/modifiers and rich actions survive. Resize is handled by App layout and screen size; close becomes the exit-request flow, not an arbitrary event queue consumer.
console.input-events.vm: same VM as the owning API

console.focus-held.wren: physical edges exist; no focus event or held-state query
console.focus-held.reason: Native focus state and physical-key held bitmap/query are not available to scripts. Tracking edges locally does not reconstruct initial held state or focus-loss recovery. Host/terminal handling does not constitute a public query/event API.
console.focus-held.vm: same VM as the owning API

console.capabilities.reason: Logical-console capabilities, backend names/build choices and frontend constraints are queryable through typed Wren catalogs/booleans. Display-specific variants describe the same owning frontend; this does not imply scripts may create/swap native displays.
console.capabilities.vm: same VM as the owning API

console.clipboard-url-caps.reason: Clipboard and URL operations exist but their native capability bits have no ScreenSupports query. Operation availability cannot be inspected in the same way as palette/pixels/font capabilities.
console.clipboard-url-caps.vm: same VM as the owning API

embedding.owner.wren: application owns menu/picker/connected VMs and routes native callbacks into Wren
embedding.owner.reason: Config console/path/audio/history/hyperlink/log/service pointers, host create/destroy/pump and synchronous prompt/trust/status hooks form the C embedding boundary. Wren implements the UI/hook bodies through script modules and owns script callbacks, not its own embedding instance. Menu selection and Session/Conn/Status/Hook/App expose useful behavior without raw VM/context lifetime control.

application.st_app_state.reason: This is a process/frontend entry or adapter, not an additional script-owned service. Startup options choose the one application/backend and VM setup. Scripts use Menu/Settings/Host/Screen for their authorized runtime behavior; no process launch/reparse/frontend ABI or raw startup callback ownership is added.

application.st_application.reason: This is a process/frontend entry or adapter, not an additional script-owned service. Startup options choose the one application/backend and VM setup. Scripts use Menu/Settings/Host/Screen for their authorized runtime behavior; no process launch/reparse/frontend ABI or raw startup callback ownership is added.

application.st_command_line.reason: This is a process/frontend entry or adapter, not an additional script-owned service. Startup options choose the one application/backend and VM setup. Scripts use Menu/Settings/Host/Screen for their authorized runtime behavior; no process launch/reparse/frontend ABI or raw startup callback ownership is added.

application.st_console_startup.reason: This is a process/frontend entry or adapter, not an additional script-owned service. Startup options choose the one application/backend and VM setup. Scripts use Menu/Settings/Host/Screen for their authorized runtime behavior; no process launch/reparse/frontend ABI or raw startup callback ownership is added.

application.st_libretro_input.reason: This is a process/frontend entry or adapter, not an additional script-owned service. Startup options choose the one application/backend and VM setup. Scripts use Menu/Settings/Host/Screen for their authorized runtime behavior; no process launch/reparse/frontend ABI or raw startup callback ownership is added.

application.st_syncterm_icon.reason: This is a process/frontend entry or adapter, not an additional script-owned service. Startup options choose the one application/backend and VM setup. Scripts use Menu/Settings/Host/Screen for their authorized runtime behavior; no process launch/reparse/frontend ABI or raw startup callback ownership is added.

application.st_terminfo.reason: This is a process/frontend entry or adapter, not an additional script-owned service. Startup options choose the one application/backend and VM setup. Scripts use Menu/Settings/Host/Screen for their authorized runtime behavior; no process launch/reparse/frontend ABI or raw startup callback ownership is added.

cterm.state.wren: CTerm / ExtAttr / LastColumnFlag / Scrollback / Font / Screen
cterm.state.reason: Every st_cterm_state scalar and nested ExtAttr/last-column state has a script getter, including palette override, margins, alternate fonts and ring metadata. Protocol emulation/encoding/RIP/PETSCII variant are configured by Profile/screen mode. CTerm.write accepts UTF-8 host text, active receive input is processed by the native terminal owner. Local key injection, doorway/music/mouse policy, screenshot and font selection have typed operations. Native lifecycle/config callbacks and several direct operations are separately assessed. Font assignments are the live CTerm.font view and the masked setFont operation; script-output Screen.font remains independent.

cterm.owner.reason: Create/destroy/config service pointers, raw wire writes/decoder feed, poll/finish/disconnect, resize/origin notifications, RIP receive framing and event routing belong to the active term session. Scripts use CTerm/Screen/Hook/Transfer on that parser rather than independently writing a borrowed decoder or holding output/input/log callback contexts. Screen-mode/Profile policy supplies config values; quiet is a host audio choice. This does not claim a standalone script terminal-emulator constructor.
cterm.owner.vm: same VM as the owning API

cterm.encoding-control.wren: CTerm.encoding/codepage are readonly; Profile.encoding configures sessions
cterm.encoding-control.reason: The native live set_encoding operation has no script setter. Reading active state or editing the profile for future initialization is not the same capability.
cterm.encoding-control.vm: same VM as the owning API

cterm.reset.wren: CTerm.write can send reset escape sequences
cterm.reset.reason: No dedicated script operation invokes st_cterm_reset_terminal or returns its native reset status. That function finishes pending input, resets parser state and rebuilds the RIP engine. CTerm.write can submit protocol reset sequences through the current parser, but does not expose this complete host reset transaction or its failure result.
cterm.reset.vm: same VM as the owning API

cterm.audio-fx.reason: Native play_fx_u8 accepts PCM effects directly; Wren has no direct script PCM submission. Terminal protocol music is not arbitrary playback coverage.
cterm.audio-fx.vm: same VM as the owning API

cterm.font-result.wren: Font.load(file[, codepage]) returns selector / FileError / FontError
cterm.font-result.reason: Loading returns the allocated selector and changes no assignments. A readable actual File owned by the current context is required. Native file failures become FileError; bitmap/mapping/capacity/capability/registration failures become FontError, with the native portable status retained separately. Wrong arguments abort. Configured/occupied selectors are reserved. Failure publishes no entry, and console-owned copied bitmaps outlive the File. Selector allocation is host policy; scripts receive the chosen selector rather than a raw console identifier.
cterm.font-result.vm: same VM as the owning API

hyperlinks.registry.reason: URI and parameter data have equivalents under typed ids and VM availability. Enumeration is not a native public registry operation. Registry creation/destruction, root marking, collection and temporary copy/free are ownership mechanisms assigned separately.

hyperlinks.gc-owner.reason: Root registration/mark callbacks, collection, create/destroy/dispose implement native reachability and copy ownership. Wren receives owned String values and ids rather than raw registry roots or borrowed memory.
hyperlinks.gc-owner.vm: same VM as the owning API

ooii.protocol.wren: term session OOII parser; CTerm.ooiiMode / Host.haveOOII/maxOOIIMode
ooii.protocol.reason: Mode query/set/limits are exposed; parser create/destroy/write and artwork/reply/sound/attribute callbacks are native protocol orchestration on the current connection. Scripts do not take ownership of a second OOII parser or raw embedded resources. Direct sound playback omission is in audio.playback.

ooii.mode.reason: Mode is clamped 0..3 and discards partial commands exactly as native set_mode. Availability is Host.haveOOII.
ooii.mode.vm: same VM as the owning API

screen.modes.reason: Native mode catalogs, current/custom mode selection and palette defaults have higher-level equivalents. Detailed console config/font/palette construction is owned by mode application; scripts select supported modes instead of allocating native descriptors. Native persistence ini_name is not a separate script display name.
screen.modes.vm: menu mode selection and connected profile metadata

history.owner.reason: Native create/destroy/publish/copy/info/capacity describe detached history retention. Settings.scrollbackLines configures capacity; the menu prepares the retained screen mode and Scrollback gives dimensions and row copies as owned Surface cells. Scripts do not publish arbitrary native history buffers or replace the application history owner.

history.clear.reason: Native history.clear has no explicit script action to discard retained history. Changing capacity or overwriting screen rows is not an equivalent clear operation. Whether scripts should control retained history is a scope decision.
history.clear.vm: same VM as the owning API

term.owner.reason: Native session/config ownership, CTerm borrowing, run/pump/disconnect, terminal/transfer/RIP reservations and raw transport/filter/capture contexts belong to the application. Scripts use Conn/Session leases/CTerm/Transfer/Hook/Capture; independent parser pumps, raw borrowed buffers and callback pointers would compete with that owner. Profiles/screen modes supply initial emulation/encoding/fonts/palette/status/RIP/throttle policy. Native encoded-text storage is translated into owned script send Operations.

term.controls.reason: Current session controls, semantic key/text sending, transfer inspection and exclusive wire claim/release/available/read have typed equivalents. Host-registered hooks carry the wire/input transformations and capture behavior; auxiliary activity is represented by SessionLease holdCount and explicit release.
term.controls.vm: same VM as the owning API

text.codepages.wren: Codepage constants/decodeByte; Font.codepage/codepageOf; Menu.encodings; semantic Conn sends
text.codepages.reason: All native codepage choices and byte-to-scalar decoding are represented. Encoding uses the current session and capability helper encodes_, not a general public encodeByte(codepage, scalar) operation. Native broken_vertical metadata has no script query. Native count/name are available through the Menu encodings catalog; enum COUNT is a native sentinel, not another encoding.

emoji.catalog.reason: Pinned catalog entries and base/variant grouping become script values; sequence count is List.count. Exact lookup is performed by the Emoji wrapper/native record workflow rather than exposing a pointer or the native count sentinel.

emoji.locale.reason: Host locale context resolves preferred languages and English fallback, then exposes catalog names/keywords/search to Emoji. Locale create/destroy and returned index allocation are host/VM ownership. Script does not instantiate an independent override language context; host preferred-language policy is the existing contract.

text.comparison.reason: Canonical caseless keys and grapheme-boundary matching are explicit Text methods; Text.compare performs native Unicode collation with case-sensitive choice. Native sort-key create/compare/destroy is a reusable optimization behind comparison, not a required raw object. Typed menu/picker validation uses the native name/wildcard policies; absent general utility methods are separately recorded.

text.compare-utilities.wren: picker masks / Menu.nameAvailable / typed model setters
text.compare-utilities.reason: No general grapheme wildcard matcher or parameterized Unicode name validator is exported. The picker and BBS/theme/font validators consume these native capabilities within fixed policies. Text.compare supplies collation, not an exact numeric result of the separate caseless-key comparison routine; caselessEqual is available for canonical equality.
text.compare-utilities.vm: same VM as the owning API

text.st_utf8.reason: Scalar property tables, decomposition/composition, decoder partial buffers/events and incremental segmentation are engine mechanisms. Text.graphemes and Screen.textWidth provide semantic results; KeyEvent/codepage APIs expose committed input. Wren Strings retain standard arbitrary-byte semantics; host text validates UTF-8 and normalizes NFC, raw payloads preserve bytes. General low-level Unicode property/decoder utility exposure is not implied by these typed interfaces.

text.presentation.reason: Normalizer/grapheme/presentation create/feed/reset/finish/peek/consume and event revision/filter callbacks belong to input/terminal/renderer owners. Text.graphemes and normalizedByteCount expose high-level analysis; script code does not own another live host scalar-filter pipeline.

text.explicit-normalize.wren: Text.normalizedByteCount and implicit NFC host boundaries
text.explicit-normalize.reason: Native st_unicode_text_normalize returns canonical UTF-8 bytes. No public Text method returns the normalized String itself; normalizedByteCount returns only size. Host normalization of config/path/display inputs is unchanged and does not normalize arbitrary Wren Strings or provide a pure return-value utility.
text.explicit-normalize.vm: same VM as the owning API

strings.native-storage.reason: strdup/strndup/strlcpy/strlcat/strtok_r are native char-buffer lifetime/capacity/iterator machinery. They are not script memory APIs; Wren owns immutable Strings and standard tokenization. All fallback declarations are force-extracted to cover capability-absent builds.
strings.native-storage.vm: same VM as the owning API

bbs.mutation-status.reason: Selected BBS native mutation and rewrite integer results are preserved in menu-only MenuError, with null on success. Pure Boolean/pointer failures retain no invented integer reason. Safe-mode and read-only policy errors have no nativeCode. Drafts, identities, generations, partial writes and optional cache policy retain their contracts. Menu.load result fidelity is assessed separately in bbs.load-status.

settings.result-status.wren: Settings apply/save/reload; Menu font/web/sort actions; MenuError; Menu.activateFonts
settings.result-status.reason: Selected action methods return null/MenuError, creators return their object/MenuError. Native portable codes and generic integer failures are kept distinct by origin; Boolean/pointer failures have no invented nativeCode. Menu.saveFonts persists only; activateFonts invokes existing native activation separately. Binding-owned preparation/runtime application preserve available native results and existing call order/partial effects. Native C signatures and storage policy are unchanged. Full native disk reload and emoji-recents errors are separate open assessments.

themes.operation-status.wren: theme operations return null/error String; document.save returns [code, message]
themes.operation-status.reason: ThemeDocument.save preserves its native document error enum, including conflict. Most other theme operations flatten native integer reasons into a diagnostic String, so callers cannot reliably branch on native I/O/invalid/not-found statuses without parsing prose. Catalog fields and editable content remain mapped.

console.operation-status.reason: Successful drawing/state behavior has equivalents, but native int-returning methods generally become void/null/Bool or a Fiber abort with text. Native IO_ERROR distinctions are not uniformly retained as typed results. Capability guards and validation exist; they do not provide a lossless native error API. Pointer releases and native void-returning lifecycle methods are not affected by this finding.
console.operation-status.vm: same VM as the owning API

text.scalar-utilities.wren: Text.graphemes / Screen.textWidth provide higher-level results only
text.scalar-utilities.reason: No general query API exposes native grapheme/Indic/pictographic/RGI-prefix properties, canonical combining class/decompose/compose, East Asian Width/emoji/default-ignorable/nonspacing properties or scalar columns. These are consumed by native text rendering and segmentation, but that use does not make individual pure queries available to scripts. General Unicode analysis is a scope decision; this records no requirement to change Wren String semantics or port Unicode tables.
text.scalar-utilities.vm: same VM as the owning API

text.strict-utf8-codec.wren: String.fromCodePoint / String.codePoints; strict host text boundaries
text.strict-utf8-codec.reason: Standard Wren can encode scalars and inspect String codepoints/bytes, but its arbitrary-byte String indexing is not the native strict decode_one result/consumed/error contract. No public strict one-shot UTF-8 validation/decode API accepts arbitrary bytes and returns that native information. Incremental decoder buffers remain host-owned. Whether scripts need a separate strict codec is a scope decision.
text.strict-utf8-codec.vm: same VM as the owning API

session.lifecycle-info.reason: Native remote_closed records drained remote termination rather than a local hangup/exit. The script callbacks and connected Bool do not expose that exact final cause. Session.holdCount counts explicit Wren leases, not the native SSH auxiliary transport liveness or every pending SFTP request. Those aggregate owner decisions are not a public inspection result; exposing a reason/liveness snapshot is a scope decision, not a second transport owner.
session.lifecycle-info.vm: same VM as the owning API

time.precision.wren: Timer.now monotonic seconds; standard System.clock CPU seconds
time.precision.reason: The usable clocks exist, but Timer.now uses the native millisecond source and returns zero on native clock failure. No API exposes the native nanosecond monotonic/CPU result and its status; standard System.clock uses the C clock() resolution rather than calling st_time_process_cpu_ns. Submillisecond/native-error fidelity is an omitted utility scope decision, not an absence of a monotonic clock.
time.precision.vm: same VM as the owning API

cterm.operation-status.reason: Text write and semantic key injection preserve successful behavior and handled/not-handled, but native status and partial consumed count become generic Fiber abort messages. The caller cannot inspect the native failure code. Raw wire/decoder ownership remains native.
cterm.operation-status.vm: same VM as the owning API

list.crypto.metadata.reason: Menu-only snapshots copy every native info field with no secrets or borrowed lifetime. All recognized cipher/format/KDF enums are named. KDF-inapplicable fields are null; absent model is distinct from plaintext. Native metadata and exact integer conversion are checked. Correct legacy names do not enable legacy writes.

fonts.load-errors.reason: Native failure origin distinguishes file I/O from invalid bitmaps, unsupported mappings and registration failures. NONE corresponds to success without an Error. Portable status is preserved as FileError.code or FontError.nativeCode; captured errno belongs only to FileError. Grant failures occur before file I/O.
fonts.load-errors.vm: same VM as the loading operation

fonts.assignments.reason: A live indexed view reads/writes each assignment, and one mask operation updates any combination together after validation and pending-output completion. Failure preserves all assignments; retained cells keep resolved fonts. The detached altFonts snapshot and singular altFont alias are removed. Script-output Screen.font slots remain independent. Indexed setter operational errors abort with FontError so they cannot be lost as assignment results.

bbs.load-status.reason: Menu.load preserves native portable failures from list opening, sorting and model construction in MenuError.code/nativeCode. Failure preserves the installed model, generation, views, grants and diagnostics; success retains existing invalidation. Obsolete MenuReadStatus/migration codes and statusMessage are removed without aliases. Native open/reload ownership and C APIs are unchanged.

settings.disk-reload.wren: Settings.reload copies current running settings; no full native disk reload action
settings.disk-reload.reason: The original result assessment grouped st_settings_reload with Settings.reload, but the native function rereads disk and the Wren method copies running settings. The approved chunk preserves the Wren reset-to-running contract. Full native disk reload and its result remain outside this chunk and open for scope review.

settings.recent-result.reason: Native st_settings_remember_emoji returns a portable integer status, but Emoji.recordUse reduces failure to a String. This existing ledger row was grouped with Settings results; emoji-recents error fidelity is outside the approved BBS/Settings/font/web/sort mutation chunk and remains open.

bbs.source-values.reason: The four native source enum values are available in the menu VM for diagnostic interpretation. Entry source detail and shadowed-record inspection remain separately Partial under bbs.provenance. BBSListType keeps its distinct two-value profile contract.

documentation_findings.reason: docs/api/bbs-entry-fields.adoc claims 50 persisted keys / 56 members but st_profile.h has 57 members, including cterm_log_level. The table omits CTermLogLevel -> Profile.ctermLogLevel, which is declared and bound. This is stale coverage documentation, not a missing binding.
